# National Geographic

> > National Geographic's exploration and science journalism covering astronomy, archaeology, wildlife photography, and natural history discoveries from around the world.

National Geographic delivers award-winning content spanning space exploration (NASA missions, exoplanets, Hubble Telescope), archaeological discoveries (Maya tombs, Jamestown, ancient Israel), wildlife photography (jaguars in Pantanal, penguins), and environmental science. The site features work from renowned photographers like Steve Winter, Frans Lanting, and Pete Muller, alongside science reporters covering breakthrough discoveries in astronomy, oceanography, and human achievement.

## Key Topics

- Space exploration and astronomy
- Exoplanets and solar system twins
- Archaeological discoveries
- Wildlife photography
- NASA missions and Hubble Telescope
- Maya civilization
- Jacques Cousteau and ocean exploration
- Kuiper belt and dwarf planets
- Instagram photography collections
- Jamestown and American history
- Pantanal and Brazil wildlife
- Sungrazing comets
- Olympic athletics and human performance
- Undersea volcanoes and oceanography

## Space and Astronomy

- [Hubble Telescope at 20: NASA Astronomers' Top Photos](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100424-hubble-telescope-20th-anniversary-pictures): NASA astronomers select top Hubble Telescope images for 20th anniversary
- [Our Solar System May Have Millions of Twins](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100108-solar-systems-like-ours-twins): Exoplanet survey finds Jupiter-Saturn analogs suggest habitable worlds
- [New Planet System May Be Most Populated Yet Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/101130-new-planets-found-solar-system-twin-science-space): HD 10180 system may be closest solar system twin with multiple planets
- [Three New "Plutos"? Possible Dwarf Planets Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/110811-three-new-dwarf-planets-pluto-kuiper-belt-space-science): Three potential dwarf planets discovered in Kuiper belt beyond Neptune
- ["Suicide" Comet Storm Hits Sun—Bigger Sun-Kisser Coming?](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/110117-comets-storm-sun-soho-nasa-sungrazing-science-space): SOHO observatory captures sungrazing comet swarm, larger comet predicted

## Archaeological Discoveries

- [Jacques Cousteau Centennial: What He Did, Why He Matters](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100611-jacques-cousteau-100th-anniversary-birthday-legacy-google): Jacques Cousteau's centennial celebrates ocean exploration and Aqua-Lung
- [100th Anniversary of Roald Amundsen Reaching South Pole—How the Grueling Race Was Won](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100th-anniversary-of-norwegian-roald-amundsen-reaching-south-polefind-out-how-the-grueling-race-was): Amundsen-Scott South Pole race centennial explores 1911 expedition history
- [Pictures: Odd Maya Tomb Yields Jeweled Teeth, More](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100721-maya-tomb-human-fingers-king-guatemala-science-pictures): Maya royal tomb at El Zotz, Guatemala reveals jeweled teeth and artifacts
- [Pocahontas's Wedding Chapel Found at Jamestown](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/101110-pocahontas-wedding-chapel-jamestown-science): Archaeologists discover Pocahontas's wedding church at Jamestown, Virginia
- [Pictures: Pagan-Cult Worship Objects Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100616-israel-pagan-cult-tomb-objects-pictures): Bronze Age pagan ritual objects discovered at Tel Qashish, Israel

## Ocean and Earth Exploration

- [Video: Giant Undersea Volcano Revealed](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100714-indonesia-okeanos-volcano-exploration-vin-video): NOAA footage reveals 10,000-foot undersea volcano near Indonesia

## Wildlife Photography and Instagram Features

- [Our Favorite Instagram Photos: Jaguar Cubs and Penguin Chicks](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/0909-favorite-instagram): Weekly Instagram highlights featuring wildlife photography from Pantanal

- [Vancouver 2010 to Be Warmest Winter Olympics Yet](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100212-vancouver-2010-warmest-winter-olympics): Vancouver 2010 Winter Olympics faces record warm temperatures and El Niño
- [Did Olympic Athletes Peak in the 1980s?](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100226-vancouver-2010-olympics-new-world-record): Study finds Olympic athletes approaching human performance limits
